scope: Independent finite review of 17 profile-dependent and 5 code-present cases; N0 synthetic development only.

historical_gdi_graph.scope: Historical graph only; not final B3 consumer proof.

unexpected_mutations_accepted: web.environment LANGUAGE traversal plus non-C LC_ALL
pure_preflight_probe.meaning: Validator accepts these mutations; shipped Compose does not contain them. Not a tenant exploit demonstration.

cases.attacker_prerequisites: Run infocmp analyze_string on attacker-controlled terminfo.
cases.existing_controls: No infocmp subprocess in inspected application/native sources; terminal type fixed server-side.
cases.remaining_condition: CLI exists; no exec allowlist prevents future trusted extension/tool use.
cases.recommendation: Keep tool invocation outside tenant data paths; removing this optional CLI with truthful inventory is a separate possible change.

cases.attacker_prerequisites: Control LANGUAGE and a non-C LC_MESSAGES locale plus a readable malicious .mo file across a trust boundary.
cases.existing_controls: Engine has fresh C.UTF-8 environment; B2 image default LANG=C.UTF-8. No tenant-to-environment writer found.
cases.remaining_condition: Web/jobs inherit deployment environment. Preflight accepts LANGUAGE/LC_ALL overrides.
cases.recommendation: Fix/validate locale variables for every role; test crafted environment rejection and no tenant-controlled catalog path.

cases.attacker_prerequisites: Native changeset_apply on crafted SQLite session changeset.
cases.existing_controls: Default supervisor requires PostgreSQL; no uploaded SQLite/SQL/changeset route found.
cases.remaining_condition: System SQLite exposes FTS5 and SESSION; Python SQLite and liblastlog2 are consumers. Developer settings fallback and alternate command are outside supervisor guarantee.
cases.recommendation: Require exact supervised command/PostgreSQL profile; forbid tenant SQLite files/SQL/changesets; test alternate-command refusal and preserve separate developer SQLite testing.

cases.attacker_prerequisites: Privileged nsenter --join-cgroup on attacker-controlled target.
cases.existing_controls: No SYS_ADMIN/host namespaces/cgroup/device mount in shipped N0 Compose; no-new-privileges; children CapEff=0 checked separately; B2 fstab has no entries.
cases.remaining_condition: mount SUID 04755 and nsenter remain present. No runtime invocation found. Qualification tooling uses nsenter --net only; that is a different host-side boundary.
cases.recommendation: Require verified caps, no-new-privileges, namespace/mount isolation and exact default command. Never run these tools on tenant-controlled paths; do not infer safe kernel version.

cases.attacker_prerequisites: Parse an attacker-supplied XML document containing nested entity expansion/DTD.
cases.existing_controls: Identified Debian consumer is Fontconfig; engine has fresh private HOME, no FONTCONFIG override, fixed font, and disabled file transfer. Rootfs/font configs are read-only in shipped profile.
cases.remaining_condition: Fontconfig parses XML; writable engine HOME exists by design. Exact Debian Fontconfig source closure and all-role configuration controls are not complete. Resource limits are not a repair.
cases.recommendation: Pin approved font configuration paths; reject configuration-shadowing mounts/env; verify actual font file consumers. Prefer reviewed ABI-compatible Expat backport for this reachable XML parser.

cases.attacker_prerequisites: Call strfmon(_l) with width and insufficient output buffer; format may be fixed.
cases.existing_controls: No strfmon import in historical ELF graph or call in reviewed FreeRDP/Guac/application source.
cases.remaining_condition: Absence of a public symbol import is not a complete indirect-call proof; deployment extensions are trusted code.
cases.recommendation: Revalidate targeted consumer closure on final image; keep user-controlled monetary formats out of native calls; do not call it patched.

cases.attacker_prerequisites: Pass crafted TSIG data into deprecated DNS record printing APIs.
cases.existing_controls: No ns_printrr/fp_nquery import in historical graph or product source. Ordinary DNS resolution is a distinct operation.
cases.remaining_condition: Deprecated functions remain in libc; future diagnostics or trusted code could call them.
cases.recommendation: Forbid tenant-directed DNS pretty-printer tooling; revalidate final consumer set. DNS timeout test does not cover these APIs.

cases.attacker_prerequisites: Privileged pathname ACL API follows attacker-controlled intermediate symlink.
cases.existing_controls: No identified product handler invokes pathname ACL API on tenant paths; native/application children unprivileged; rootfs read-only.
cases.remaining_condition: cp/install/mv/sed/tar in B2 really import affected APIs. Tool execution/backup traversal must remain outside tenant-controlled paths.
cases.recommendation: Verify backup/restore use exact owned synthetic paths; no privileged recursive copy/ACL operation over tenant filesystem input. Do not equate absent ACL CLI with absent library APIs.

cases.attacker_prerequisites: Authenticated Kerberos client sends mismatched delegated KRB-CRED arrays to a GSS acceptor.
cases.existing_controls: Default product paths are outbound RDP/LDAP/libpq clients; LDAP uses simple bind after StartTLS; no GSS acceptor listener found.
cases.remaining_condition: libgssapi imports krb5_rd_cred; WinPR contains an acceptor routine despite server=OFF. B3 ASN.1 patch is not this CVE fix; real Kerberos acceptor/delegation is unqualified.
cases.recommendation: Keep acceptor/delegation endpoints absent and verify final listener/source profile. If server-side GSS is introduced, backport vendor fix and test malformed KRB-CRED before use.

limits: No new runtime exploit or Docker/PG/NAS test was executed.
Selected regular paths were read from archive layers without filesystem extraction, following links or executing ELF. This selected-file reader is not a whole-filesystem sentinel.
ELF import searches and source searches are not full control-flow proofs.
Historical image and source hashes cannot replace final B3 image rescan/profile verification.
Metadata/public JSON is unsigned analysis evidence, not independent build or human identity attestation.
No memory/CPU cap, no-dsa, unfixed status or passing transport test is treated as a vulnerability fix.
B3 makecheck KEYRING/KDB/DNS omissions are separate unqualified capabilities, not assurance for these 22 cases.
